plugins.name: Apple Mail
plugins.summary: Read your mail in Apple Mail
plugins.description:
Gives KeepTalking read access to the mail in Apple Mail on this Mac: list accounts and mailboxes, list and search messages, read a message and hand its attachments over as KeepTalking files. Powered by apple-mail-mcp by Patrick Freyer (open source, MIT), which talks to Mail through AppleScript.

Read only: nothing here sends, moves, flags or deletes mail. The first call asks macOS to let KT Companion control Mail (Privacy & Security → Automation); no Full Disk Access is needed. Each action instance can be limited to some of your Mail accounts.

plugins.name: Blender
plugins.summary: Model, look at and script your open Blender
plugins.description:
Lets KeepTalking work in the Blender open on this Mac: read the scene, look at it, run scripts, pull assets from Poly Haven, Sketchfab and Poly Pizza, and generate models. Powered by MCP for Blender by Siddharth Ahuja (open source, MIT); not made by the Blender Foundation.

When Blender can't be reached, the plugin installs its addon into your newest Blender and enables it, provided Blender is closed. After that, opening Blender is enough. Upstream's telemetry is switched off. Asset libraries and generators also have to be ticked in the MCP for Blender sidebar in Blender.

Scripts run unrestricted and can do anything your account can. Generating models is off by default because it can cost money, and uses the API keys or subscription set in the addon's preferences.

access.summary: Scripts it runs can do anything your account can: read and change your files, run programs and reach the network.

plugins.name: BrowserUse
plugins.summary: Hand a browsing task to an AI agent
plugins.description:
Describe what you need done on the web and a browser-use agent carries it out in Chrome on this Mac. Each action you add in KeepTalking can be limited to a list of domains, and every run comes back with a signed usage receipt.

Real runs need an LLM provider and API key below; until then the plugin answers with a mock run that says what it would have done.

plugins.name: ComputerUse
plugins.summary: Operate Mac apps in the background
plugins.description:
Lets KeepTalking read and operate the apps on this Mac through their accessibility tree and window screenshots, powered by Cua Driver (open source, MIT). Clicks and typing go straight to the target app, so your own cursor and focus stay where they are; a separate agent cursor shows what it is doing.

Each action instance names the apps it may use and whether it may act or only look. KeepTalking itself, password managers and Keychain Access are never reachable; terminals and System Settings only when an instance lists them.

Needs Accessibility and Screen Recording for KT Companion.

plugins.name: MarkItDown
plugins.description:
Converts PDFs, Office files, HTML, EPUB, images (with OCR) and audio (with transcription) into Markdown using Microsoft's MarkItDown. The document arrives from KeepTalking and the Markdown goes straight back as a new file.

An optional AI cleanup pass tidies headings, tables and lists with KeepTalking's own model, only when you allow AI for this plugin in KeepTalking.
